sections.h2: Navigating Working Capital & Cash Flow in Nepal
sections.contentHtml:
In Nepal's commercial landscape, profitable businesses frequently struggle with cash flow due to extended debtor cycles, advance import requirements, and seasonal surges such as the Dashain-Tihar festival period. Our consultancy equips founders and executives with actionable tools to maintain robust liquidity.

Rolling Cash Forecasts

Weekly and monthly rolling cash projections ensuring payroll and supplier obligations are met without emergency borrowing.

Break-Even & Margins

Rigorous contribution margin analysis identifying profitable product lines and cutting unproductive overhead.

Management Dashboards

Clear monthly executive summaries translating complex ledgers into key performance indicators (KPIs) for leadership.

sections.h2: Distinction Between Financial Consulting and Auditing
sections.contentHtml: It is vital to distinguish management consulting from statutory auditing. Statutory audits are external compliance reviews conducted after the close of the fiscal year (Ashad 31) to certify that financial statements comply with Nepal Financial Reporting Standards (NFRS) for the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) and Office of Company Registrar (OCR). Business financial consulting is proactive and internal: we work alongside management throughout the year to structure strategies, optimize profitability, and prepare clean records before the auditor arrives.

faqs.question: Why is cash flow forecasting critical for small businesses in Nepal?
faqs.answer: Nepal operates heavily on credit sales with unpredictable settlement timelines, while suppliers and staff require fixed disbursements. A rolling cash forecast exposes upcoming liquidity deficits 6 to 12 weeks in advance, enabling management to take corrective measures before a crisis emerges.

faqs.question: How do you help prepare loan proposals for commercial banks in Nepal?
faqs.answer: We assist businesses in compiling historical financial trends, debt service coverage ratio (DSCR) calculations, projected balance sheets, and cash flow models required by Nepalese commercial banks for working capital and term loans.
